feeds.title: Criminal Element - Original crime stories, exclusive excerpts, blog posts, giveaways
feeds.description: Criminal Element is a community website featuring daily content for fans of the crime and mystery genres in all of their forms. The site features original short stories and excerpts from upcoming crime and mystery novels along with daily blog articles.

feeds.title: Crime Fiction Lover - The site for die hard crime & thriller fans
feeds.description: Book reviews, features, author interviews, news and more! Whether you love psychological thrillers, pulp, cosy mysteries or Nordic noir, Crime Fiction Lover has something for you...

feeds.title: Crime Reads
feeds.description: CrimeReads is a culture website for people who believe suspense is the essence of storytelling, questions are as important as answers, and nothing beats the thrill of a good book. It's a single, trusted source where readers can find the best writing from the worlds of crime, mystery, and thrillers.

feeds.title: The Venetian Vase
feeds.description: The Venetian Vase started as a supporting site for two books: 100 American Crime Writers and 100 British Crime Writers. The blog is edited and maintained primarily by Steven and Chris Routledge. Read Book reviews, Interviews, and funny little strolls down the Crime Fiction lane.

feeds.title: Crimespree Magazine
feeds.description: Founded in 2004, Crimespree is an award-winning print magazine that covers all aspects of crime fiction, including books, movies, DVDs, comics and more. It features interviews with authors, articles about crime fiction and also articles by authors.

feeds.title: Sleuth Sayers
feeds.description: A criminally compelling web site by professional crime writers and crime fighters.

feeds.title: JOFFE BOOKS
feeds.description: Joffe Books an independent UK publisher of high-quality fiction. News from Joffe Books about publishing, books, ebooks, kindle. Crime thrillers, mystery and thriller publisher. Best sellers. Publishers similar to Bookouture.

feeds.title: Jim Fisher True Crime
feeds.description: Welcome to the Jim Fisher True Crime blog, a place for people interested in crime, criminal investigation, policing, law, writing, and forensic science.

feeds.title: Promoting Crime Fiction
feeds.description: From an early age I have been a lover of crime fiction. Discovering like minded people at my first crime conference at St Hilda's Oxford in 1997, I was delighted when asked to join a new group for the promotion of female crime writers. In 1998 I took over the running of the group, which I did for the next thirteen years.

feeds.title: Murder is Everywhere
feeds.description: Ten renowned crime writers blog from different corners of the world.

feeds.title: The Rap Sheet
feeds.description: The Rap Sheet has earned its reputation as an essential resource for readers seeking information about what's new and interesting in the world of crime fiction. It covers crime, mystery, and thriller fiction both recent and vintage, appearing in all media--print as well as broadcast. Edited and written mostly by J. Kingston Pierce, the site has been nominated twice for Anthony Awards.

feeds.title: Cross Examining Crime
feeds.description: On this blog, Crossing Examining Crime, I plan to mainly review crime fiction. I also enjoy reading translated crime fiction. I will primarily be reviewing books, but occasionally I will comment on films, TV series and theatre productions. I also write articles for CADs (Crime and Detective Stories) magazine and Mystery Scene Magazine.

feeds.title: George Kelley
feeds.description: George Kelley is an expert on crime fiction, and in fact, donated his extensive pulp and paperback fiction collection to the University of Buffalo at the State University of New York.

feeds.title: Crime Time - There's always time for Crime.....
feeds.description: Reviews, Features and News about the best crime fiction in the UK and around the world

feeds.title: Raven Crime Reads
feeds.description: Have a good wander across Raven Crime Reads for reviews and crime news. The blog author with nom de plume is Raven spends all their free time reading and reviewing books across a range of genres preferably crime for many major publishers and online sites.

feeds.title: Crime Watch - Investigating crime fiction from a Kiwi perspective
feeds.description: News and Musings on international crime and thriller fiction, with a New Zealand flavour

feeds.title: Criminal Minds
feeds.description: Each week the crime fiction authors of Criminal Minds respond to a question about writing, reading, murder and mayhem.

feeds.title: Chapter In My Life
feeds.description: Hi and welcome to Chapter In My Life - my blog about all things books! My name is Sharon. I am a Scottish Blogger with a particular interest and love of Scottish Crime Fiction. I read daily and on average devour 2/3 books per week (more if time permits). In particular I love Crime/thrillers/police procedurals and especially Scottish Crime Fiction

feeds.title: The Crime Segments
feeds.description: The crime segments is part of my overall online book journal -- it's neither a literary nor expert take on crime fiction/mysteries, but rather a way to keep a record of my reading as I explore different authors, different subgenres and currently works from obscure writers.

feeds.title: Nobody Move!
feeds.description: John DuMond writes true crime and crime fiction. His stories have appeared in the webzines Jake Magazine, Flashing in the Gutters, DZ Allen's Muzzle Flash, Powder Burn Flash, Defenestration, and the ebook anthology Discount Noir.

feeds.title: Kittling Books
feeds.description: Hi! I'm Cathy, and I'm addicted to books (especially crime fiction), laughter, and traveling off the beaten path. In Kittling: Books, I chart my reading, sharing reviews of what I've read, and hoping to encourage others to read the books I've loved. You won't just read favorable reviews here. If I don't like something I've read, I'll say so, and I'll explain why I didn't like it in as kind a manner as I know-how.

feeds.title: Do You Write Under Your Own Name?
feeds.description: Martin Edwards' Crime Writing Blog . I've published eighteen crime novels, most recently Gallows Court. I received the Poirot Award for my contribution to the crime genre, and have won the CWA Short Story Dagger and CWA Margery Allingham Prize.

feeds.title: Type M for Murder
feeds.description: Rick Blechta, John Corrigan, Barbara Fradkin, Hannah Dennison, Frankie Bailey, Aline Templeton, Charlotte Hinger, Thomas Rendell Curran, Mario Acevedo and Donis Casey — always ready to Type M for MURDER.

feeds.title: Crime Book Junkie
feeds.description: In Crime Book Junkie, Noelle shares her thoughts and reviews on Crime fiction, psychological thrillers, action thrillers, horror, murder mysteries, and further Book-writing adventures. Author Noelle Holten is an award-winning blogger at www.crimebookjunkie.co.uk.

feeds.title: Do Some Damage
feeds.description: Do Some Damage is a group of crime writers, each with a different voice and something to say. From grizzled vets to grizzly rooks, they pull back the curtain on the way the industry works.

feeds.title: Murder in Common
feeds.description: All about crime fiction books and authors. Mainly, I feature books by debut and mid-list writers. While not quite reviews, I consider these books to be recommended reading and try to give the flavour of each story.

feeds.title: BOLO BOOKS
feeds.description: This blog will focus on books in the mystery and thriller genre. Crime fiction is my passion and I want to share that with you.

feeds.title: The Invisible Event
feeds.description: The Invisible Event is my attempt at compiling all that i have to say about Crime Fiction books and authors. Hi, I'm Jim Noy and I love to read classic crime fiction. I'll usually try most things from the Agatha Christie era and will commit to definitely reading something if it features an impossible crime.

feeds.title: A Crime is Afoot
feeds.description: Welcome to The Game's Afoot, now A Crime is Afoot. My name is Jose Ignacio. In my spare time, I developed a taste for classic and contemporary crime fiction. The purpose of this blog is just to keep track of the books I read.

feeds.title: Steph Broadribb
feeds.description: Crime Thriller Girl leads a double life: I'm a thriller writer, writing as Steph Broadribb and Stephanie Marland and an avid reader of all things crime thriller. My blog is about books and being a writer, and I love to connect with people who share a passion for crime thrillers too.

feeds.title: Hooked From Page One
feeds.description: I'm Jacob and I have been an avid reader for as long as I can remember. Recently I have discovered a true passion for crime fiction and psychological thrillers. On my blog you'll mainly find reviews for crime and psychological thriller novels. I take part in blog tours and I sometime feature author interviews, guest posts and giveaways.

feeds.title: SHOTS
feeds.description: SHOTS is a web magazine and blog exploring the annals of the Crime Fiction scene in the UK. Discover reviews of crime and thriller books, interviews, and news about various authors and their books in the latest blog updates.

feeds.title: Beneath the Stains of Time
feeds.description: Welcome to the niche corner, dedicated to the great detective stories of yore and their neo-classical descendants.

feeds.title: A Crime Readers Blog
feeds.description: This blog started as a challenge to read as many books as I could by authors who were appearing at the Harrogate Crime Writers Festival. Once that was over I realised that I enjoyed writing this blog nearly as much as the actual reading, so have kept it going.

feeds.title: Cath Staincliffe Blog
feeds.description: Cath is also a scriptwriter, creator of ITV's hit police drama, Blue Murder, starring Caroline Quentin, which has sold worldwide in places as diverse as Fiji, Iceland and Yemen. Cath is writing a series of stand-alone novels where ordinary families find themselves caught up in extraordinary events. Cath is a founder member of Murder Squad, a virtual collective of northern crime writers.

feeds.title: Little Big Crimes
feeds.description: Blog on The best mystery story and books I read this week

feeds.title: International Noir Fiction
feeds.description: International Noir Fiction includes reviews and ideas on crime novels (mostly from outside the U.S.)

feeds.title: Hawley Reviews
feeds.description: 'm Alex Hawley, avid reader and fan of crime. I enjoy reading and reviewing books, in particular audio books, as I am dyslexic. My intention with this reviewing blog is to discuss the different world of the audio book and the different approach this may give to the written word.

feeds.title: Ron Franscell Blog
feeds.description: Ron Franscell's books have earned high praise from bestselling authors. His book reviews and essays have been widely published in many of America's biggest and best newspapers, such as the Washington Post, Chicago Sun-Times, San Francisco Chronicle, Denver Post, San Jose Mercury-News, St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel and others.

feeds.title: Vintage Crime - Crime and spy fiction from Poe up to 1950
feeds.description: Vintage Crime community is for discussion of crime novels and detective fiction from the beginning (with Edgar Allan Poe) up to the 1960s.

feeds.title: Only Detect
feeds.description: Here you'll find reviews of books- most of them detective novels-that I have read over the years. I will be posting them according to no particular logic and in no specific order. My choice of books to read follows no particular logic, either. Clue-driven puzzle mysteries (think Agatha Christie) and attitude-driven hard-boiled tales (think Dashiell Hammett) appeal to me equally.

feeds.title: Indie Crime Scene
feeds.description: A blog for all things mystery, crime fiction, noir, suspense and thrillers.

feeds.title: Crime Fiction Writer
feeds.description: Michael Bracken, an award-winning writer of fiction, non-fiction, and advertising copy, has received multiple awards for copywriting, two Derringer Awards for short fiction, and the Edward D. Hoch Memorial Golden Derringer Award for lifetime achievement in short mystery fiction. The author of several books and more than 1,200 short stories, he has edited five crime fiction anthologies and provides editorial services to book and periodical publishers.

feeds.title: Chrissie Poulson Blog
feeds.description: Writer of the Cassandra James crime novels and short stories, art historian. Before Christine Poulson turned to crime, she was a respectable academic with a PhD in History of Art and had written widely on nineteenth-century art and literature.

feeds.title: Crime Writer Sue Coletta - Inside the mind of a crime writer Blog
feeds.description: Member of Mystery Writers of America and Sisters in Crime. I love all things crime, and have always been fascinated by how the criminal mind works. In my books, I offer an honest look behind the crime scene tape. Sometimes it can be frightening; sometimes it can be fascinating. Are you ready to take the ride?

feeds.title: Crime by the Book
feeds.description: Crime by the Book CBTB is a book review blog dedicated to investigation of the crime fiction genre. Crime book reviews and recommendations, covering the newest psychological thrillers, mysteries, Nordic Noir, and more.

feeds.title: The Crime Fiction Writer's Forensics Blog
feeds.description: The Crime Fiction Writer's Forensics Blog is Science of Crime and the Art of Fiction by DP Lyle. He is an Award-winning Author, Lecturer, Story Consultant

feeds.title: Historical True Crime Detective
feeds.description: Historical True Crime Detective, where you will discover forgotten crimes and criminals lost to history. This blog is the official website for true crime writer Jason Lucky Morrow, author of four books including the popular series: Famous Crimes the World Forgot, Volume I and Volume II.

feeds.title: Mark McGinn Blog
feeds.description: Features Mark McGinn's books as well as reviews of other authors' works. Mark is a Christchurch crime/thriller writer who helps other crime writers tell great stories.

feeds.title: AustCrimeFiction
feeds.description: Well it's basically a database of Authors and Books from Australasia (Australia, New Zealand, and nearby areas) AND a blog AND a running commentary (on the rare occasions when I feel brave enough to post an article). It's also the place where I post book reviews. A big percentage of the books I read will be from local authors (books that are covered under Books & Writers here).

feeds.title: COL'S CRIMINAL LIBRARY
feeds.description: Thoughts on books I've read. I have a soft spot for small and indie published crime fiction. Not averse to read self published books either. It's not all about big names and mainstream crime fiction.

feeds.title: The Crime Warp
feeds.description: We are a group of avid crime readers and aspiring crime fiction writers. We met at Harrogate Crime Writers' Festival and decided to work together to share our enthusiasm for the genre in the form of book reviews, author interviews, quizzes & trivia and of course some samples of our own writing.

feeds.title: Crime Worm
feeds.description: Crime Worm is author and blogger Linda Boa's outlet for news and book reviews. She particularly likes to support Scottish crime writers, small imprints, and new authors, although she enjoys high-profile books too. She also writes about Irish crime fiction and feels there are many great Irish writers working at the moment.

feeds.title: Scandinavian Crime Fiction
feeds.description: Reads and reviews various crime fiction books.

feeds.title: In Reference to Murder Blog
feeds.description: A crime fiction blog with news, tips, interviews, book and author profiles, and over 3,000 links chosen with both mystery readers and mystery writers in mind.

feeds.title: Chris Longmuir, Crime Writer
feeds.description: Crime writer, Dundee Book Prize winner,5 published crime novels, 1 historical saga, and guides on how to self=publish. Techno geek.

feeds.title: Crime ALways Pays by Declan Burke
feeds.description: Author, editor and journalist, although rarely in that order. Irish crime fiction, Irish mystery fiction, Irish thrillers, Irish crime writing.

feeds.title: Crime Thriller Fella
feeds.description: I write. I write screenplays and novels -- and hopefully I'll have a bit of news on that front in due course. This is me thinking aloud about what I read, and maybe it'll give me a bit of space to occasionally show what I've learned. Tell me about your favourite crime thriller novels and movies and such like. Tell me about new stuff and old stuff. Crime movies, TV and movies. Because I want to immerse myself in it. I want to learn.

feeds.title: Crime Scene NI
feeds.description: Gerard Brennan's short stories have appeared in numerous anthologies, including The Mammoth Book of Best British Crime. His novella, The Point, was published by Pulp Press in October 2011 and won the 2012 Spinetingler Award.

feeds.title: Crime Time by Mathew Paust
feeds.description: Author, reader, editor and blog posts on crime and mystery books.

feeds.title: Billy Helston
feeds.description: Billy Helston. Writer. True crime books. Research and images. London, Victorian and Edwardian murderers and criminals.

feeds.title: Adventures in Crime Fiction Land
feeds.description: The author reads crime fiction novels and reviews about them.

feeds.title: Chillers Killers and Thrillers
feeds.description: Aspiring Crime/Thriller writer just finished studying MA Crime Thriller Novels at @CityUniLondon / Book Blogger / Bookworm / Biscuit Muncher/ Music Lover

feeds.title: Crime Fiction Ireland
feeds.description: Crime Fiction Ireland chronicles the growing crime fiction scene in Ireland on page and screen. We are also partial to Nordic Noir and Eurocrime, and cover Irish true crime books from time to time.

feeds.title: Fair Dinkum Crime
feeds.description: The aim of the site is to celebrate Australian crime fiction with reviews, news, interviews and anything else we think is relevant. Our definition of Australian crime fiction is pretty broad so we try to cover all the sub genres of books written by Aussie authors (set anywhere) and books set in Australia

feeds.title: Crimezine - #1 for Crime
feeds.description: Crimezine the web based home for all that rocks in the world of crime fiction. The main focus of this site is books, movies, and television shows. But the real world apocalypse of true crime shenanigans is never too twisted or bizarre for the true crime fan so I will include that too.

feeds.title: A short walk down a dark street
feeds.description: A short walk down a dark street provides weekly links to what's fresh, what's famous, and what's fiendish in short mystery and crime fiction. I anticipate I'll post something new near the end of each week or on weekends.

feeds.title: Crime Scraps Review - All about crime fiction
feeds.description: Crime Scraps Review which is a compendium of my reviews and thoughts mostly about crime fiction, but very occasionally about the biggest criminals of all, the politicians. Most of my recent reading has been translated crime fiction but I do read historical crime novels, British, American and Australian crime fiction as well.

feeds.title: Past Offences - Classic crime, thrillers and mystery book reviews
feeds.description: The best mystery and crime fiction (up to 1987): Book and movie reviews

feeds.title: Detectives Beyond Borders
feeds.description: This blog is a proud winner of the 2009 Spinetingler Award for special services to the industry and its blogkeeper a proud former guest on Wisconsin Public Radio's Here on Earth. In civilian life I'm a copy editor in Philadelphia. When not reading crime fiction, I like to read history. When doing neither, I like to travel.

feeds.title: The Reader Is Warned
feeds.description: I'm Dan, an artist, writer and comedian based in London, and a hoarder of impossible crime fiction.This blog is dedicated to musings and philosophisings on the reading, writing and collecting of impossible crimes and locked room mysteries.

feeds.title: True Crime
feeds.description: True Crime Stories in the news from around the world. Strange Crime News, FBI Most Wanted, Amber Alerts, Top 15 Most Wanted by U.S. Marshals, National Sex Offender Website. True Crime News Updated 24 hours a day.

feeds.title: True Crime Diva
feeds.description: True Crime Diva is a personal blog that discusses true crime cases. I focus mostly on missing people and unsolved murders and prefer to write about older cases.

feeds.title: Euro Crime
feeds.description: Euro Crime reviews the latest books and its other features include a comprehensive bibliography section, a summary of upcoming titles, author websites, details of events, links to newspaper reviews, crime fiction award results and an occasional competition.

feeds.title: Rowmark Blog
feeds.description: the official website of international crime author Pauline Rowson. The website for crime author Pauline Rowson featuring her crime novels, thrillers, business books, events, news, book signings and guest appearances.

feeds.title: The Crime Review Blog
feeds.description: The Crime Review has been created to explore my favourite genre: crime fiction. You will likely notice a focus on UK/Europe/Scandinavian crime fiction. A mystery lover's exploration of the best reads in the crime genre.

feeds.title: Janet Roger Blog
feeds.description: Literary Crime Fiction author, traveler, art historian, lover of film, theater, classical music & all things historical.

feeds.title: Jane Isaac - UK Crime Fiction Writer, Amazon Bestseller
feeds.description: Jane Isaac is a crime fiction author from rural Northamptonshire. Her novels include the DI Will Jackman Series and DCI Helen Lavery Series, available on Amazon.

feeds.title: The Crime Writers' Association
feeds.description: For all lovers of crime fiction and non-fiction. Books, events, and news from authors of the Crime Writers' Association. The Crime Readers' Association offers a unique perspective on the largest community of crime writers in the world: the Crime Writers' Association.

feeds.title: Femmes Fatales
feeds.description: Ferociously talented women dedicated to the fine art of crime fiction.

feeds.title: TheCrimeHouse - Everything crime fiction
feeds.description: TheCrimeHouse is a website for people who love crime fiction, thrillers and murder mysteries. Here you find reviews, interviews, news, and much more.
